title: Thyroxine (T4) Test
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Measures thyroxine, the main hormone the thyroid makes. Free T4 is the active form that reaches the tissues; total T4 measures free and bound together. Free T4 is considered more accurate and is used more often. A T4 result alone cannot diagnose a thyroid problem, so it is usually paired with TSH.
low: A low T4 may be a sign of hypothyroidism, Hashimoto's disease, certain stages of thyroiditis, a pituitary problem, too much or too little iodine, congenital hypothyroidism, or treatment for hyperthyroidism or thyroid cancer.
high: A high T4 may be a sign of hyperthyroidism, Graves' disease, certain stages of thyroiditis, toxic goiter or nodule, too much iodine, a non-cancerous pituitary tumour, or taking too much thyroid hormone medicine.
notes: Severe illness and medicines such as birth control pills and steroids can affect T4. Results are read alongside other thyroid tests.
